        🎲 What is this game?

        You wake up locked in a rusty cell. In the cell: a slot machine 🎰 and an ATM 🏦 showing a debt you owe a demonic captor. At the end of every deadline, the ATM must hold enough deposited coins to cover the debt. Pay it, and the debt grows. Fail, and the trapdoor under your feet opens — down you go. 🕳️ The developers stress it is a rogue-lite horror game, not real gambling, and it never asks for real money.

        The machine is meant to be broken: charms, phone deals and bank interest are all tools for bending the odds until a run snowballs out of control. ❄️➡️💰

        🖱️ Controls

        First-person point-and-click: look around the one-room cell and click the thing you want — pull the lever to spin, press the red button on top to fire charged charms, click the ATM to deposit, the shop cabinets to buy, the telephone to answer, the toilet, drawers, key box and door. PC is effectively mouse-driven; console versions move a focus cursor with the stick; Switch 2 supports mouse controls.

        ⚠️ Honest gap: no source publishes a reliable key-by-key control table (the one “controls” page found was generic and untrustworthy), so this book describes controls by what they do instead of inventing key bindings.

        🏠 The cell — your whole world

        • 🎰 Slot Machine — 5 columns × 3 rows; lever on the side; red button on top; a floppy disk on the machine shows 666 (remember that disk — it matters later 🙈); a toy phone recalls past phone picks.
        • 🏦 ATM — deposit coins toward the debt; shows debt, deposited amount and current interest.
        • 🛍️ Shop — glass cabinets with 4 charm slots; charms cost tickets 🎟️; paid restocks cost coins 🪙.
        • 🗄️ 4 Drawers under the shop — storage with a strange afterlife (see 🧟 Corpse in the Walkthrough).
        • 📞 Telephone — rings once per deadline from Deadline 2 onward.
        • 📋 Symbols Board & Patterns Board — the in-game reference charts, on the wall.
        • 💻 Computer — database of locked/unlocked charms and their unlock conditions. This is the real campaign.
        • 🔑 Key Box — locked glass cabinet that holds the door key once earned.
        • 🚽 Toilet — “take a leak” / “take a dump”; a wall display tracks toilet completion. Yes, really. Use it. 👇
        • 📰 Magazines by the toilet = the credits, with an overall completion stat. Plus a Settings Cabinet and a giant number painted on the wall (it feeds the Ascension achievement).

        🔁 How a run works — step by step

        1. 🪙 Run start: 13 coins in hand, 2 tickets, 30 coins already deposited. Deadline 1's debt is 75 — you need 45 more deposited coins.
        2. 🚽 Use the toilet immediately. “Take a leak” unlocks the charm Number 1, “take a dump” unlocks Number 2 (both join the shop pool), and doing both earns the achievement Corpore Sano. 🏆
        3. 🎟️ Pick your round format: each deadline has 3 rounds. Before a round choose Most Spins — 7 spins, 1 ticket at round end, or Fewer Spins — 3 spins, 2 tickets at round end.
        4. 🎰 Pull the lever. Each pull costs the current lever price (7 coins on Deadline 1, rising per deadline — full table in 💀 Deadlines). Wins pay coins into your hand. Can't afford the lever? “Underspin” rules shrink your spins proportionally; at 0 coins you get one free pull.
        5. 🏦 Deposit at the ATM whenever you like. Deposited coins are safe and earn interest; coins in hand are what a 666 can steal.
        6. 🛍️ Spend tickets in the shop between (and during) rounds. Free restock at each new deadline; paid restocks cost coins and get pricier within the same deadline, then reset. Charms can be discarded/resold for part of their ticket value.
        7. 📞 Answer the phone when it rings at the start of a deadline (Deadline 2+): pick 1 of 3 offered abilities, reroll the offers for tickets, or choose “Be Right Back” to shelve the decision.
        8. 💹 End of round: the ATM pays interest on your deposited balance (base 7%), round-end tickets land, red-button charms regain 1 charge.
        9. ⏰ End of deadline: deposited total covers the debt → debt paid, bigger debt appears, plus a Deadline Bonus for finishing early: coins = 6 × the deadline number, + 4 tickets per round skipped. 🎁 Doesn't cover it → alarm, red lights, trapdoor — run over (unless a save effect like the Ankh fires; surviving this moment is the Near Death Experience achievement). A new run restarts at Deadline 1, debt 75.
        10. 🎯 Long-term goals inside a run: earn drawer keys (Deadlines 4–7), assemble the corpse, and eventually earn the door key. Details in 💀 Deadlines and 🚶 Walkthrough.

The slot machine dominates the frame, its display glowing with a huge red 666. Pinned Polaroid-style photos speckle the wall; a red-cross motif (the Holy Book) sits on the shelf; at the lower right sits the white Maneki-neko Lucky Cat 🐱 figurine with red ears — the game's mascot charm.

        Logo treatment: “CLOVER PIT” in chunky white block capitals, the second line rendered as three slot-reel windows showing red clovers — the third reel splattered with blood. 🍀🍀🩸

        Tagline: “A rogue-lite slot machine nightmare. Gamble for your life in a never-ending debt simulator!”

        🧮 The scoring formula — learn this first

        Every scoring pattern pays: Symbol Value × Symbols Multiplier × Pattern Value × Patterns Multiplier. Both multipliers start at ×1, and charms/phone calls raise them. Because the four factors multiply, raising your lowest factor is usually the best value — and Patterns Multiplier increases are scarcer, so +1 Patterns Multiplier is typically worth more than +1 Symbols Multiplier. 📈

        🎰 Symbols (grid is 5 × 3 = 15 positions)

        SymbolBase valueBase chance
        🍋 Lemon219.4%
        🍒 Cherry219.4%
        🍀 Clover314.9%
        🔔 Bell314.9%
        💎 Diamond511.9%
        🧰 Treasure (chest)511.9%
        7️⃣ Seven — 👑 the king77.5%
        😈 Six (the 666) — hidden—special, below

        Demo-era guides call Treasure “Coins / Gold Coin” — Treasures replaced Coins after the betas; Treasure is the current name.

        ✨ Symbol modifiers (a scored symbol can carry one)

        • 🌟 Golden — permanently raises that symbol's value by its base value.
        • 🪙 Token — pays out half your current Interest amount in coins.
        • 🎟️ Ticket — pays 1 ticket.
        • 🔁 Repetition — retriggers every pattern containing that symbol.
        • 🔋 Battery — restores 1 charge to a random Red-Button charm.
        • ⛓️ Chain — permanently raises its pattern's value by the pattern's base value.

        Natural affinities: Lemon/Cherry lean Token/Repetition · Clover/Bell lean Ticket/Battery · Diamond/Treasure/Seven lean Golden/Chain. The Unholy Fusion DLC adds four more: Investor (+1% interest until round end when scored), Rising (Symbols Multiplier +1 until deadline end), Copy (copies the nearest other modifier), Revenge (pays back 5% of all coins you've lost to 666s this run).

        😈 The 666 — and the 999

        • From Deadline 3 onward, every spin has a base 1.5% chance to roll a 666, checked independently of Luck after everything else.
        • Deadlines 3–6: a 666 wipes all coins earned that round that you haven't deposited. Deadline 7+: it wipes all coins you are holding. Deposited coins are always safe. 🏦
        • 🙈 In Sacred Mode the roll becomes a 999 instead — which pays your round's earnings a second time. (How to reach Sacred Mode lives behind the spoiler gate in 🏁 Endings.)
        • Charm interactions: Holy Bible converts an incoming 666 into normal symbols (then 50% chance to discard itself); Rosary does the same on a 35% random trigger; Demon's Horn turns a 666 into Luck +10 on the next spin; Gabihbb'h doubles Symbols Multiplier for the round after a 666; Book of Shadows grants decaying bonus spins after a 666; Necronomicon raises 666 chance by +3% for Patterns Multiplier +2. 📕

        🔷 Patterns

        There are no pair / two-of-a-kind payouts by default — patterns start at 3 symbols. Larger patterns suppress smaller patterns contained inside them (except Jackpot).

        PatternShapeBase value
        HOR3 in a horizontal line ➡️×1.0
        VER3 in a vertical line ⬇️×1.0
        DIAG3 on a diagonal ↘️×1.0
        HOR-L4 horizontal×2.0
        HOR-XL5 horizontal (full row)×3.0
        ZIGzig-zag of 5 ⚡×4.0
        ZAGzag-zig of 5 ⚡×4.0
        ABOVEupward triangle 🔺×7.0
        BELOWdownward triangle 🔻×7.0
        EYEeye / diamond formation 👁️×8.0
        🎉 JACKPOTall 15 positions the same symbol×10.0
        • 😇 The Sacred charm Angel's Hand can temporarily add 2-symbol patterns (HOR-S, VER-S, DIAG-S) worth ×0.5.
        • 🏆 Ultimate Jackpot (for Super Mega Ultra Ultimate Win): a Jackpot pattern repeated at least 4 times in the same spin resolution.
        • 🍀 Luck: each point of Luck forces one grid position to become a chosen symbol. 7 Luck guarantees at least a 7-symbol match · 10 Luck guarantees a win (unless a 666 overrides) · 15+ Luck guarantees a Jackpot (unless a 666 overrides).

        📊 Debt growth by deadline (log scale — each ring ≈ ×10; a linear chart would be one flat line and one skyscraper)

        ♾️ Scaling past Deadline 9 — there is no final deadline

        • Debts continue endlessly, formula-driven (from the decompiled code, game v1.2): past Deadline 9 the base debt explodes by a compounding formula, then gets multiplied by +5% per equipped corpse/skull piece and doubled under Delusions of Grandeur. A “winning” run is defined by the key and the door 🚪, not by clearing a last debt.
        • Restock base cost from Deadline 10 = debt ÷ 20. Each further paid restock in the same deadline raises the cost by (current cost ÷ 5, rounded down, min +1); the price resets each deadline.
        • The lever price follows its own formula — roughly 2 × (deadline − 1), scaled up by a factor that grows every 5 deadlines.

        🗄️ Drawer keys — exactly one per run

        Completing Deadline 4 → key 1 · Deadline 5 → key 2 · Deadline 6 → key 3 · Deadline 7 → key 4. One drawer per key. Four winning-progress runs open all four drawers (and unlock the DLC's Surgery Machine). 🔑🔑🔑🔑

        🚪 The door key — and the famous “250,000”

        Once all four drawers are unlocked and all five corpse pieces (4 limbs + Skull) are equipped, a key deadline is scheduled: 3 deadline completions after the corpse conditions are met, and no earlier than the 7th–8th deadline completion. In practice this lands on Deadline 8 (base debt 200,000) — and the corpse set's +25% debt penalty makes it 250,000. That's why most guides just say “clear the 250,000 deadline.” Clear it, and the Skeleton Key appears in the Key Box. 🗝️ What the key's colour decides is behind the spoiler gate in 🏁 Endings.

        ⚠️ Flag: one AI-generated guide prints Deadline 4 as 2,333 — wrong; 2,222 is correct (wiki + walkthrough + decompiled guide agree). Two sloppy guides also misprint Deadlines 7/8 as 125,000 / 300,000; correct: 66,666 / 200,000.

        Steam advertises “150+ items”; the official wiki table is the source for every number below (costs are tickets 🎟️). Rarities run Common / Uncommon / Rare / Legendary. Many charms are unlockable — they only enter the shop pool after a lifetime condition is met, which makes the charm-unlock system the game's main meta-progression alongside drawers and Memory Cards. 🔓

        🪑 Charm space

        • Base table space: 7 charms. “Doesn't take space” charms ignore the limit; corpse pieces use their own slots.
        • ➕ Increases: Property Certificate +2 (while equipped), Cardboard House +1 (permanent, once per run), Beach Hotel +3 (DLC fusion), the phone call “Please don't throw my stuff away!” +1 permanent (once per run).
        • ➖ Decreases: Nuclear Button −1, Megaphone −1, Hourglass −1 (while equipped); the Sacrifices Memory Card lowers base space 7 → 6.
        • Theoretical maximum ≈ 20 (23 on First Love, 19 on Sacrifices).

        🎲 Charm traits (random modifiers on charms themselves)

        Florid (+2 coins at deadline end) · Avid (Symbols Mult +1) · Ambitious (Patterns Mult +1) · Obsessive (the last pattern of a spin triggers once more) · Gambler (1 free restock per deadline) · Speculative (+3% interest) · Devious (+0.6% chance of a 666 😈). Random traits appear once you've finished ≥3 runs, unlocked a drawer, or reached your 2nd debt; Devious never rolls randomly before a drawer is unlocked; instant charms never get traits.

        🂡 The Aces & the Pictures 🖼️

        • ❤️ Ace of Hearts (3) — whenever 3+ patterns score, Lemons & Cherries permanently rise by base value.
        • ♣️ Ace of Clubs (3) — Clovers & Bells rise permanently per 3 tickets spent in the shop.
        • ♦️ Ace of Diamonds (3) — any 4+ symbol pattern permanently raises Diamonds & Treasures.
        • ♠️ Ace of Spades (3) — every 7 charm triggers across rounds permanently raises Seven.
        • All four Aces unlock by opening 2 drawers and dying; fusing all four (DLC) makes the Poker Deck 🃏 — score every base symbol in a round → double all symbol values permanently.
        • 🖼️ Pictures (Red Button, 4 charges, recharge 1/round): Lemon Picture (2), Cherry Picture (2), Clover Picture (3), Bell Picture (3), Diamond Picture (4), Treasure Picture (4), Seven Picture (4) — each makes its symbol manifest +2 more often for the rest of the deadline.

        🌟 “Golden [symbol]” charms & modifier dealers

        • Golden Lemon / Cherry / Clover / Bell (3/3/3/3): +20% chance that symbol rolls with the Golden modifier. Golden Diamond / Golden Treasure (2/2): +25%. Golden Seven (1): +30%.
        • 🪙 Token dealers: Bricks (Lemon +20%, 1), Wood (Cherry +20%, 1), Sheep (Clover +15%, 2), Wheat (Bell +15%, 2), Stone (Diamond +10%, 2), Harbor (Treasure +10%, 2), Thief (Seven +10%, 2).
        • 🎟️ Ticket dealers: Wheelbarrow (Lemon +20%, 4), Shoe (Cherry +20%, 4), Thimble (Clover +20%, 2), Iron (Bell +20%, 2), Car (Diamond +20%, 3), Ship (Treasure +20%, 3), Tuba Hat (Seven +20%, 3).
        • 🌐 Global dealers (3 each): Naughty Dealer (Token chance for any symbol, +5% growing to 15%), Greedy King (Golden, +3% → 25%), Raging Capitalist (Ticket, +5% → 25%), Clicker (fruit Repetition +15%), AA Batteries (Clover/Bell Battery +6%), Crystal Sphere (Diamond/Treasure/Seven Chain +12%) — plus the decaying trio Personal Trainer (+25% Repetition, −5%/round), Electrician (+5% Battery, −1%/round), Fortune Teller (+25% Chain, −5%/round).

        🔴 Red-Button & charge charms

        The machine's red button fires every charged charm at once; charges refill +1 at each round end. Key pieces: Number 1 (3; from taking a leak 🚽) — yellow-symbol patterns (Lemon, Bell, Treasure, Seven) trigger an extra time this round · Number 2 (3; from taking a dump) — same for non-yellow symbols (Cherry, Clover, Diamond) · Midas Touch (3) — all scored symbols permanently rise by base value this round · Ring Bell (2) — Symbols Mult +1 permanently per use · Weird Clock (5, 11 charges) — +1 round this deadline · Cross (4) — flips between a growing Patterns Mult passive and +3% 666 chance · Car Battery (2, no space) — instantly refill all charges · Dynamo (2), Super Capacitor (4), Electricity Meter (4), Potato Battery (1) — charge-generation engines · Nuclear Button (4) — all Red-Button charms trigger twice, −1 space · Sacred Heart (Sacred) — 50% chance the button consumes no charges. 🔋

        😈 666 / occult charms

        Holy Bible (1), Rosary (1), Demon's Horn (2), Necronomicon (3), Book of Shadows (2), Gabihbb'h (2), Baphomet (3 — each 666 permanently doubles Above/Below pattern values), Cross (4), Magical Tomato (3), Ritual Bell (1), Crystal Skull (2), Possessed Cell Phone (1, Red Button 3 charges — force a 666 on the next spin, Deadline 3+), Chastity Belt (3 — Patterns Mult +1 for every Red Call you picked up and refused), Evil Deal (50, above). 📕

        🎲 Utility, dice & oddities

        Dear Diary (2, +1 phone option), Megaphone (7, phone abilities trigger twice, −1 space), D4 (2, random 30%: reroll non-pattern symbols), D20 (5, round end: replace drawer charms with random new ones), Jimbo (5, random effect — a Balatro crossover joke charm 🃏), Photo Book (1, no space: restock the shop with Pictures), Fortune Cookie (1, no space: restock with Luck charms), Fruit Basket (4, fruit patterns trigger twice, 10 rounds), Eye Jar (2), Nose (3), Voicemail (2, Symbols Mult +1 per phone reroll this run), Pain Killers (3, a lone pattern's symbols become your most valuable symbol), Little Star (3), Depression (1, kills Spontaneous Luck — a tech pick), 7 Sins Stone (2), Necklace (1), CloverBell (1), Sardines (1, a joke charm whose only power is double resell value — its description admits it was added because a random video comment asked for sardines 🐟).

        🛟 Survival charms

        • ☥ Ankh (2) — when you are about to die, gain 2 extra rounds, then discard it. Unlock: die 3 times.
        • 🐴 One Trick Pony (2) — grants a guaranteed Jackpot next round, then discards. Unlock: die 5 times.
        • 📼 Music Tape (5, no space) — immediately gain 1 extra round this deadline.
        • ☀️ Ra's Book (DLC fusion) — random 40%: if you are dying, fully pay the debt and advance. Fuse Holy Bible + Ankh.

        😇 Sacred charms (0 tickets — spawned only by Sacred/white phone calls)

        Angel's Hand (adds 2-size patterns), Eye of God (an Eye pattern re-pays all coins earned from 999s this run), Holy Spirit (each 999 applies a random trait to all table charms), Sacred Heart (button may not consume charges), Halo (a lone pattern converts adjacent symbols to its symbol), The Blood (Repetition/Battery/Chain chances), The Body (Token/Ticket/Golden chances), Eternity (each 999 adds pattern repetitions), Adam's Ribcage (each 999 doubles Patterns Mult for the round), Ophanim Wheels (each 999 makes the next spin a Jackpot). ✨

        🧟 Corpse pieces (see also 🚶 Walkthrough)

        Corpse — Left Arm, Right Arm, Left Leg, Right Leg (0 tickets, cannot be discarded, +5% debt each, discarded if left sitting in a drawer at a deadline's end) and Skull 💀 (1 ticket, bought from the shop once the four limbs are held; +5% debt; at each deadline start it spawns a free random charm in an empty drawer for every corpse piece equipped). Full set = +25% debt.

        🧪 Surgery (fusion) charms — Unholy Fusion DLC

        The Surgery Machine (unlocked once all 4 drawers are open) fuses charms; fusion cost rises per use, ingredient charms are banned from the shop while the result is equipped, and results have 0 resell value. 30 fusion charms — highlights: Garbage / Trash Can / Dumpster (fuse any 2/3/4 charms: permanently raise all symbols / Symbols Mult +1 / Patterns Mult +1, no space) · Cosmic Cat (Lucky+Chonky+Swole Cat) · Poker Deck (all four Aces) · 10 Fingers Hamsa (both Hamsas) · Bullet Train (both Locomotives — doubles both multipliers after a no-interest round) · Mad Emperor (the three modifier dealers) · Exotic Matter (battery family — Red-Button charms fully recharge before every spin, but each button press doubles the debt ⚠️) · Glorious Trumpet (Horseshoe+Nuclear Button+Sacred Heart) · Beach Hotel (Property Certificate + Sardines — +3 charm space 🏖️) · VIP Card, Magic Potion, RWD Cart, Graded Card, Booster Pack, Black Hole, Cat Toy, First Place Trophy, Old One's Sigil, Amalgama, Platinum Record, Black Pepper. The four corpse fusions and Apocalypse are behind the spoiler gate. 🙈

        💊 Consumables & one-time items

        There is no separate “pills” inventory — the consumables are the “Doesn't take space” charms: Clover Voucher (+4 tickets), Lost Briefcase (30% of debt in coins), Car Battery (refill charges), Crowbar (+3 free restocks), Fortune Cookie / Photo Book (themed restocks), Music Tape (+1 round), Cardboard House (+1 space), Cigarettes (permanent symbol growth + restock), Garbage (DLC). Expired Meds and Pain Killers are the pill-themed charms. Skulls: the corpse Skull and the Crystal Skull. 💀

        ⚠️ Flag: a few charm numbers differ between the Fandom wiki and the official wiki.gg (e.g. Grandma's Purse +15% here vs +25% on Fandom; Bricks/Wood Token +20% vs +35%; Cigarettes cost 1 here vs 3 in secondary guides; some Picture prices). This book prints the official wiki.gg figures throughout.
        • 🔔 Rings at the start of every deadline from Deadline 2. Base offer: 3 abilities (Dear Diary makes it 4).
        • 🔄 Reroll cost: starts at (current deadline − 1, minimum 1) tickets and rises +1 per reroll, resetting each deadline.
        • ⏸️ “Be Right Back” shelves the call — crucially, for Red calls the game only registers a refusal if you actually picked the phone up first. (This matters enormously — see 🏁 Endings 🙈.)

        ⚪ Normal calls (white text) — always positive, modest

        • 🗄️ “Please don't throw my stuff away!” — +1 charm space permanently, once per run. Take this when offered.
        • 💚 “Can I borrow some green?” — +5 tickets.
        • 🏷️ A call that discounts shop charms by 2 tickets until the next restock.
        • 🏷️ Trait-stamping calls — stamp Florid / Avid / Ambitious / Obsessive / Gambler / Speculative onto a random equipped charm.
        • 🔋 A call restoring all Red-Button charges.
        • 🍋 Seven “manifest” calls that permanently raise one symbol's frequency by +1 (“Life gave me lemons,” etc.).
        • 🔷 Calls raising the values of small (≤3-symbol) or large (4+-symbol) patterns; a call doubling Jackpot value. 🎉

        🔴 Red / Evil calls (red text) — strong, with a catch

        Accepting one permanently kills Sacred Mode for the run 🙈. Guaranteed on Deadlines 3 and 7, and forced whenever you scored a 666 in the previous (non-skipped) round before first picking up the phone. Examples: double your tickets but coins → 0 · double your coins but tickets → 0 · two shop charms free but tickets → 0 · random traits on all shop charms plus a Devious trait on one of your charms · “My head hurts!” (fires all other currently offered abilities, then stamps Devious on a random equipped charm). 😈

        ✨ Sacred / Holy calls (white phone, gold text)

        Only in Sacred Mode 🙈; one is forced the moment 999 unlocks. Examples: Symbols Mult +3 · Patterns Mult +1 · Red-Button charms permanently need 1 less charge (min 1, pickable twice) · patterns trigger once more, permanently · “Help!” — spawn a Sacred Charm but halve your coins · a call that modifies all shop charms and makes one free.

        🧩 DLC phone charms

        With Unholy Fusion, Evil calls can also spawn the eleven “sin” charms — Sloth, Limbo, Lover 1, Lover 2, Gluttony, Avarice, Rage, Heresy, Violence, Fraud, Treachery — 0-ticket Legendaries built around the Revenge modifier and 666s. 😈

        💾 Memory Cards — the run modifiers

        • Unlocked via Memory Packs, available after Drawer #2 is opened. A pack is offered at the start of a deadline when you hold enough coins to pay the current and next deadline outright; accepting commits those coins (declining, pulling the lever, or dropping below the threshold cancels the offer).
        • One card is chosen per run as a run modifier. Escaping with a card active turns it Golden Holographic ✨ and unlocks Hard Mode for that card; escaping Hard Mode turns it Rainbow Holographic 🌈. Making every card Rainbow is the Lord of the Pit achievement — the hardest in the game.
        ⚠️ Flag — Hard Mode maths: the current wiki (v1.2) says Hard Mode raises the debt by a cumulative +25% per deadline starting from 0%; an older walkthrough says it simply doubles deadlines, and a cheat-site submission says Rainbow takes three wins. The wiki version is printed here; the disagreement is flagged, not hidden.

        🧟 Drawers and the corpse

        • Charms stored in an unlocked drawer at the moment you die 💀 are transformed: next run, those drawers contain corpse pieces instead.
        • Rolling a 666 can also drop an unequipped corpse piece into a drawer (replacing what's there).
        • 🧺 The farm: fill all four drawers with any cheap charms and deliberately die to farm the set.
        • ⚠️ Equip all four pieces promptly — a piece left in a drawer at a deadline's end is discarded. Then buy the Skull 💀 from the shop to complete the set (+25% debt total) and unlock the key schedule.

        🟢 Phase 0 — Your first ever run

        Use the toilet (both options 🚽). Take Fewer Spins rounds, bank everything, pay Deadline 1 (75) and Deadline 2 (200). Die whenever it happens — dying 3 times unlocks the Ankh, 5 times the One Trick Pony, and every death teaches the loop. 💀 Check the computer 💻 to see charm unlock conditions; they are the real campaign.

        🎰 Phase 1 — Deadlines 1–3 (75 / 200 / 666)

        Prioritise tickets (Fewer Spins = 2 tickets) while debts are tiny. Buy one focused engine: a Picture + Golden charm for a single common symbol (Lemon or Cherry are cheapest to build), or an early Lucky Cat 🐱. Deposit aggressively — interest at 7% of a growing balance is your second engine. Deadline 3 introduces the 666 😈: keep undeposited cash low late in rounds.

        🔑 Phase 2 — Deadlines 4–7 (2,222 / 12,500 / 33,333 / 66,666): the key grind

        Completing D4, D5, D6, D7 across runs earns the four drawer keys. In these runs, pivot from ticket-farming to scaling: Grandma's Purse + Stonks on a big balance, Pentacle/Tarot for multipliers, or a Token build that prints half-interest per scored symbol. Answer normal phone calls freely; think hard before any red one 📞. When the phone offers the charm-space call, take it.

        🧟 Phase 3 — Corpse assembly

        With drawers open, stuff all four with cheap charms and die on purpose. Next run, equip the four corpse pieces before the first deadline ends, then buy the Skull 💀. Accept the +25% debt.

        🙈 SPOILER GATE — true-ending setup lives in here

        Phase 3 has a second, hidden job if you're going for the true ending. Nothing is visible until you tap.

        Simultaneously with corpse assembly, start refusing Red calls: guaranteed on Deadlines 3 and 7; force a third by scoring a 666 in the last round before answering (Possessed Cell Phone / Devious traits / Heartbreak card). Pick the phone up, choose “Be Right Back,” and never touch it again that deadline — each refusal burns one “6” off the machine's 666 floppy disk. Full ritual in 🏁 Endings.

        🚪 Phase 4 — The key deadline (usually Deadline 8, 250,000 with corpse penalty)

        Your build must now be an economy engine, not a slot build: interest on a seven-figure balance, Lucky Cat family payouts, or a ticket-multiplier stack (Cloverpet + Lost Wallet). Pay it, take the key 🗝️, open the door, cross the bridge, and finish. (What happens next depends on the key — spoiler gate in 🏁 Endings.)

        🏁 Phase 5 — Post-game

        Replay with Memory Cards to turn them Golden (escape) then Rainbow (escape on Hard Mode). Chase the remaining achievements 🏆, then the DLC: open the Surgery Machine, build toward the secret finale 🙈, and use Endless Mode for score-chasing — debts scale by formula forever. ♾️

        🏦 Interest, exactly — the money rule that matters most

        • The ATM pays 7% of your deposited balance at the end of every round. (The “Interest” figure the Lucky Cats pay out is this same per-round amount.)
        • 💹 Raisers: Stonks +5% · Grandma's Purse +15% decaying 3%/round · Speculative trait +3% · Evil Deal ×2 · A New Investment card +2% per deadline (max +16%, paid at deadline end instead) · DLC Investor-modifier symbols +1% until round end each. Rentier achievement = reach 30%+ interest in a run. 🏆
        • 🛡️ Deposited coins are protected from 666s; hand coins are not. The core habit: after reserving lever money and planned restock coins, deposit everything.
        ⚠️ Flag: one beginner-tips site claims 10% interest. The official wiki says 7% — 7% is what this book uses, and the disagreement is flagged, not hidden.

        🎟️ The ticket economy

        • Income: round-end choice (1 for 7-spin rounds, 2 for 3-spin rounds), Ticket-modifier symbols (1 each), Clover Voucher (+4), phone calls (+5), deadline bonus (4 per skipped round), Cloverpot interest-on-tickets at deadline end.
        • Spend on: charms (tickets), phone rerolls (tickets, rising) — not shop restocks. Restocks are coins 🪙. Mixing those two up is the classic beginner confusion.
        • 🐖 Hoarding tickets is itself a build: Cloverpet (Symbols Mult per 5 held) and Lost Wallet (Patterns Mult per 15 held) reward a fat wallet; the Scrooge achievement wants 100+ held.

        🏗️ Recommended builds (community consensus)

        • 🍋 Golden Fruit (early, reliable): build around Lemon or Cherry — Golden Lemon/Cherry + matching Picture + Ace of Hearts + Fruit Basket; cheap, common, and scales permanently.
        • 🏦 Interest Bank (mid/late): Lucky Cat → Chonky Cat → Swole Cat with Stonks and Grandma's Purse; deposit far beyond the debt (e.g. bank ~50k against a 12.5k deadline) and let per-round interest payouts dwarf spin winnings.
        • 🎟️ Ticket Merchant (late): Shoe/Wheelbarrow Ticket-modifier charms + Cloverpot + Cloverpet + Lost Wallet; hold hundreds of tickets so multipliers and rerolls are effectively free.
        • 😈 666 Cult (expert / true-ending adjacent): Devious traits, Necronomicon, Book of Shadows, Gabihbb'h, Baphomet, Evil Deal; trigger 666s on the first spin of a round (nothing earned yet = nothing to lose) and harvest their bonuses; the Cultist achievement wants 10%+ 666 chance.
        • 🔴 Red Button engine: Pictures + Number 1/2 + Midas Touch with Dynamo/Super Capacitor/Electricity Meter keeping charges full; Nuclear Button / Glorious Trumpet to double-fire.

        📞 Phone strategy

        • Normal calls are free value — take them. Bank a call with “Be Right Back” when a trait-stamping call is coming and you want it to land on a specific (cheap, sacrificial) charm rather than a corpse piece.
        • For Evil calls that zero a currency: pause the call, go spend that currency first, then come back and accept. 💸
        • 🙈 On a true-ending run, treat every red call as a refusal ritual: pick up → “Be Right Back” → never touch it again that deadline. Never picking it up at all does not count.
        • Don't reroll the phone or shop with the currency your build scales on (e.g. don't burn the tickets feeding Cloverpet). 🔥🎟️

        🚫 Common mistakes

        1. Holding cash into Deadline 7+ — a 666 takes everything in hand; deposit. 🏦
        2. Accepting one Red call on a Sacred run — the whole run's true ending is gone. 🙈
        3. Spreading upgrades across all seven symbols instead of stacking one. 🎯
        4. Chasing Symbols Multiplier while Patterns Multiplier sits at ×1 — raise the lowest factor. ⚖️
        5. Paying inflated restock prices late in a deadline — the price resets next deadline; wait if you can. ⏳
        6. Leaving corpse pieces in drawers past a deadline end — they're discarded; equip immediately. 🧟
        7. Ignoring the deadline bonus — finishing early pays 6 × deadline-number coins + 4 tickets per skipped round, so over-banking early is doubly rewarded. 🎁

        🧠 Advanced techniques (from the decompiled mechanics guide)

        • 🔮 Luck prediction: the machine's “Spontaneous Luck” spins follow learnable patterns — the first deadline's lucky spins follow one of five fixed spin-number sequences, and later lucky spins recur roughly every (4 + completed deadlines) spins (±1). Sparks ✨ telegraph them (beware: “pity” sparks after 4 dry spins also glow, with +5 Luck and +1 per further miss). Save Rotated Hamsa / Ancient Coin / Red Shiny Rock / Golden Horseshoe for a predicted lucky spin and stack them.
        • 💾 Memory Pack farming: deposit to just below the two-deadline threshold, grow interest for a few rounds, then top up and take the pack offer at the next deadline start.
        • ❄️ Cold Affection drawer farming: its 12 starting tickets buy four cheap charms to fill drawers before a deliberate death.
        • 📕 Holy Bible farming: the Bible neutralises 666s, letting you farm Memory Packs and 666-adjacent unlocks (Possessed Cell Phone needs 7% 666 chance) with less risk.

        🚫 Cheat codes: there are NONE

        CloverPit has no cheat codes, no console commands, no debug mode and no unlock codes. Nothing of the kind appears on the Steam page, in either wiki, or in any guide. The two best-known “cheat” sites' CloverPit pages (Cheatbook, GGmania) contain zero codes — only player-submitted ending/Memory-Card strategy text. This book will not print fake “cheat” lists. 🙅

        • ⚠️ The only cheat tool that exists is third-party and unofficial: CloverMod on Nexus Mods — an in-game cheat/QoL menu (press M; Insert is its recovery key) that requires the BepInEx mod loader, can alter runs and save data, and carries a corruption warning. Listed here as “use at your own risk,” not as a game feature.
        • ⚠️ Trainer sites also list a “CloverPit trainer,” but their published cheat lists are generic filler (e.g. “unlimited stamina” in a game with no stamina) and are not trustworthy.

        💥 Documented exploits & glitches (legit-system manipulation unless noted)

        • 🔮 Luck-spin prediction — intended mechanics, expertly exploited (see 💡 Tips, Advanced).
        • 📞 Forced Red calls — Possessed Cell Phone / Heartbreak manufacture a last-round 666 and guarantee next deadline's Red call (needed for Sacred Mode and Chastity Belt).
        • 🎺 Infinite charm loop (genuine bug): the developers' own Instagram showcased a run soft-locked in a never-ending spin (balance display in scientific notation); commenters identified the loop pieces as Glorious Trumpet + Sacred Heart + Golden Horseshoe — red-button charms re-firing each other indefinitely.
        • 💀 Death as a tool: deliberate deaths convert drawer charms to corpse pieces and unlock death-gated charms (Ankh, One Trick Pony, and the many “open N drawers and die” unlocks).
        • 🌱 Seeds: seeded runs exist for practice/routing but grant no achievements or endings — not an exploit path.

        🥚 Secret interactions & easter eggs

        • 🚽 Toilet: leak → unlock Number 1; dump → unlock Number 2; both → Corpore Sano. No source documents flushing items/charms down the toilet — there is no item-flush interaction in any wiki or walkthrough; one low-quality tips page uses “flushing the toilet” as loose wording for using it. The corpse goes in the drawers, not a sewer, and no hidden rooms were documented anywhere.
        • 🐟 Sardines exists purely because a random commenter on a dev video asked for sardines (its in-game text admits this).
        • 🃏 Jimbo — a nod to Balatro's mascot Joker.
        • 📰 Magazines = credits, with an overall completion percentage; the wall's giant number feeds Ascension / the Weird Clock unlock; graffiti above the phone (“Don't trust everyone”) hints at the Sacred path 🙈; the DLC adds a poster for the devs' other game RACCOIN to the cell.

        🔓 Unlockables summary

        • Charms: ~150+ in the pool, most gated behind lifetime feats listed on the in-game computer — dying (3×/5×), opening drawers and dying, discarding charms (50/100/200/300), scoring modified symbols in bulk, buying Pictures/Peppers repeatedly, reaching symbol value 1000+, losing 1M/100M to 666s, holding 30+ tickets, discovering all Memory Cards, opening the door (once / on Delusions of Grandeur). Full conditions are in 🧿 Charms A–Z.
        • Hard Mode: per Memory Card, unlocked by escaping with that card (turning it Golden Holographic ✨); Rainbow Holographic 🌈 for escaping on Hard Mode.
        • 🙈 Golden Knob: a spoiler-adjacent unlock — its how-to sits in 🏆 Achievements and 🏁 Endings.

        30 achievements on Steam and Xbox alike — 1,000 Gamerscore on Xbox, ~50–60 hours estimated for full completion. 🎮 Howard's own Xbox progress on this chapter lives in 🎮 Gamer Profiles.

        Everything in this section is spoiler content, and per the book's rule none of it is visible until you tap a gate open. Each ending has its own gate. 👇

        🙈 SPOILER GATE 1 — Ending 1: the standard ending

        Requirements and what happens when you use the key. Hidden until you tap.

        Bad / standard ending (Skeleton Key, dark key). Requirements: all 4 drawers open; all 5 corpse pieces equipped; clear the key deadline (250,000 = Deadline 8's 200,000 × 1.25 corpse penalty).

        What happens: Door → bridge → a lift whose controls are another slot machine. Use it: credits. You have not escaped — the pit just gave you a new machine. 🎰♾️

        🙈 SPOILER GATE 2 — Ending 2: the true ending (999 / Sacred)

        The full Sacred Mode ritual and the escape. Hidden until you tap.

        True / good ending (Sacred Key, white key; the “999 ending”). Everything in Ending 1, plus Sacred Mode: during the run, refuse 3 Red (Evil) phone calls — pick up the phone, choose “Be Right Back,” never pick it up again that deadline, and never accept any Evil perk (one acceptance locks you out for the run). Each refusal burns/scratches out one “6” on the machine's 666 floppy disk.

        Red calls are guaranteed on Deadlines 3 and 7; force the third by scoring a 666 in the last round before answering (Devious-trait charms, the Possessed Cell Phone charm, or the Heartbreak Memory Card). Then answer the phone on a later deadline: it turns white with gold text, the disk reads 999, and the key turns white. For the rest of the run 666s become helpful 999s (paying your round's earnings a second time). Clear the same key deadline with the white key.

        What happens: the lift has a normal button panel. Flip the switch: you rise out of the pit into open sky/sunrise 🌅; credits roll over a serene, heaven-like scene. A genuine escape. 😇

        ⚠️ Flags: one Steam ending guide phrases this as “skip the Devil phone 4 times” — it counts the final white call as the fourth; the three-refusals-then-white-call account above is the version supported by the wiki, the mechanics guide and the walkthrough press. TV Tropes additionally claims the true ending involves having lost money to a 666 at least once — no mechanics source confirms this; treat it as unverified colour, not a step.
        🙈 SPOILER GATE 3 — Secret finale: Apocalypse (Unholy Fusion DLC)

        The DLC's hidden finale and its fusion recipe. Hidden until you tap.

        Secret finale — Apocalypse. Own the DLC; unlock the Surgery Machine (all 4 drawers open); in one run fuse the four corpse-based Surgery Charms — Sacrifice (Corpse Left Arm + Cross), Resurrection (Corpse Right Arm + Ankh), Sin (Corpse Right Leg + Evil Deal), Eternal Rest (Corpse Left Leg + Weird Clock) — then fuse those four into Apocalypse and equip it.

        What happens: equipping Apocalypse kills you immediately, plays a special cutscene in which the unseen cosmic entity watching you comments on your choice, and starts a new run keeping the same Memory Card and every charm that was on your table — a New-Game-Plus ending rather than an escape. 🌌

        🙈 SPOILER GATE 4 — Death: is it an ending?

        What failing a deadline really is. Hidden until you tap.

        Death is not an “ending.” Fail any deadline without a save effect and the trapdoor drops you; the run ends and you restart at Deadline 1. Deaths are also progress: dying unlocks charms (Ankh at 3 deaths, One Trick Pony at 5) and is required to convert drawer charms into corpse pieces. 💀🔁

        ⚠️ Open questions — flagged, not hidden

        1. Interest rate: 7% (official wiki, used here) vs 10% (one beginner-tips site).
        2. Grandma's Purse: +15%, −3%/round, cost 2 (wiki.gg, live) vs +25% (Fandom). Wiki figure used.
        3. Charm numbers, Fandom vs wiki.gg: Token-modifier percentages (Bricks/Wood +20% wiki vs +35% Fandom), Cloverpot's formula, Cigarettes cost (1 wiki vs 3 in secondary guides), Picture costs. Wiki.gg figures used throughout; a full A–Z re-verify against the live wiki table is due at print time.
        4. Deadline 4: 2,222 (wiki/walkthrough/mechanics) vs 2,333 (one AI-generated guide). 2,222 used.
        5. Skeleton-Key deadline: “250,000” in most guides = Deadline 8's 200,000 × 1.25 corpse penalty; the underlying rule is a scheduling rule, not a fixed 250k debt.
        6. Red-call count: “refuse 3, the next call is white” (wiki/mechanics/walkthroughs, used) vs “skip 4 times” (one Steam guide, counting the white call).
        7. Hard Mode maths: cumulative +25%/deadline (wiki, v1.2) vs “doubles deadlines” (older walkthrough) vs “win 3 times for Rainbow” (cheat-site submission).
        8. DLC counts: wiki lists 7 DLC Memory Cards and 30 fusion charms + 11 phone charms; one DLC review says 3 new Memory Cards; launch press says “10 new charms.” Wiki preferred.
        9. True-ending extra condition: TV Tropes claims having lost money to a 666 is part of the true ending; no mechanics source confirms it. Unverified.
        10. Exact keyboard controls: no reliable source; controls are described functionally only.
        11. Cover art fine detail: described from the official key art as reproduced in press/social posts and the wiki backdrop; the Steam capsule file itself was not re-opened live during research, so colour/composition details are corroborated but not pixel-verified.
        12. 999 payout wording: “pays the round's earnings again” (multiple sources); some phrasing suggests it doubles only the triggering spin's context — the round-earnings version is the majority account.
        13. Low-quality SEO guide farms (AI-Owl, FindingDulcinea, OfZenAndComputing, Gemelog, Spot.Monster) contained multiple wrong numbers and invented statistics; they were used only where corroborated by the wiki, Fandom, Adventure Gamers, DualShockers, TrueAchievements or the decompiled Mechanics guide.

          🌐 Open the hosted book

          2. 📦 The full downloadable APK — via PWABuilder (the remaining step — no APK exists yet) Go to pwabuilder.com and run the book file address above through it (not the site root — the root is a redirect stub). PWABuilder generates the Android package: a signed APK you can sideload straight onto the Fold, plus an AAB — the AAB is only needed for a Google Play listing, which would additionally need a Play developer account; it is not required for a personal install. Bubblewrap is the equivalent command-line route, driven by the same manifest:
            bubblewrap init --manifest=https://aquatrinityx.github.io/ultimate-strategy-guide/manifest.webmanifest → bubblewrap build
          3. 🔄 Updates arrive with new editions — no new APK The packaged app always loads the live hosted book, and the service worker is network-first for pages, so each future edition re-uploaded to the same address is picked up on next open — new chapters arrive without rebuilding the APK or reinstalling. Only a name/icon/start-address change would justify re-packaging. 📖✨ (The book content updates this way; the gamer-profile numbers are snapshots baked into each edition, because a static book can't hold an API key or poll an account on its own — live sync is the master app's job.)
          4. 🧩 One honest deployment note — Digital Asset Links For a fully chrome-less packaged app (no browser address bar), the Android package's assetlinks.json must be hosted at the domain root: https://aquatrinityx.github.io/.well-known/assetlinks.json. That address lives in Howard's separate aquatrinityx.github.io user-site repo — not in this project repo, so it can't be placed from here. Without it the installed app still works, but may show a browser address bar; with it, the app opens fully standalone.
